On VTES-L, "David L. Teskey" <tes...@MEENA.CC.UREGINA.CA> wrote:
> I was playing a classic Malk Stealth-Bleed, and my friend was playing a
> Tzimice deck with plenty of Auspex-type intercept. I was bleeding with
> Gilbert Duane (My favoured heavy-hitter), and he was matching my stealth
> with intercept, point for point. The last piece of stealth I had in hand
> was the superior version of Bonding (Giving me the +1 stealth I needed but
> having the restriction of +1 bleed and no further +bleed cards for that
> action.)
>
> Here's the problem. Is there a window of opportunity for me to play a
> Command of the Beast in Superior form to give that bleed a little extra
> punch and still be successful?

Yes. Play Command of the Beast to boost the bleed (without gaining the
restriction against boosting it further). At this point, you are
still being blocked, since you haven't increased your stealth.

Then play Bonding for +1 bleed and +1 stealth.
